update.title: OT-07.2: fear in the body, the hands (Lam 4:6), woven (#2160)
update.strand: open threads on completed clusters (#2160), OT-07.2 (M01)
update.researcher_instruction: "I am still finding that you analysis and interpretation are very binary. reading Lam 4:6 is a a verse that connect wringing of hands with fear ..." Then: "#2168 approved: amend rule 73 and its guide with the three points. Then weave OT-07.2 as proposed in v2 section 4." (2026-10-19)
update.method: FE-85 (Lam 4:6), held since fear unit 2, read outward from the verse (#2168, guide v2): the clause read in the Hebrew (hul, 'to twist, writhe', with 'hands', literally 'hands did not writhe in/on her'); hul's range from strong_meaning_tree and its ESV renderings in verse_lexical; a set-based pull of verses where a hand word stands with the writhing/anguish words, with the neighbouring verses read (Isa 13:7-8; Eze 7:17; 21:7; Jer 30:6; Zep 3:16; Neh 6:9; 2Sa 4:1; Isa 35:3; Job 4:3; Heb 12:12). Woven: 10.12 v14 new section Fear in the body; Ch 11 v37 bullet Writhing and a Lam 4:10 case under Distress turns people both ways; Ch 2 v27 Lam 4:9 in Life weighed; 10.10 v32 Lam 4:10 after Lam 4:3-4.
update.claims_changed_note: Eight new claims (fear in the body and the hands; the Lam 4:6 and 2Sa 4:1 translation notes; hul's range; Lam 4:9; Lam 4:10).
update.not_woven_note: Lam 4:6's comparison of punishments goes to M56 as a forward item (not read). The wider pull with the feeble-hands word (H7503) and the melting heart (H4549) was not run.
update.quote_note: added lines checked against iba.db verse (ESV): 10.12 16 parts, Ch 11 11, Ch 2 3, 10.10 6. The two flagged parts are the gloss 'to twist, writhe', a word meaning, not a quote.

new.text: Fear and anguish are shown in the body, and the verses see them first in the hands: hands fall at a report, grow feeble as the heart melts, and are held as in labour
new.beyond_text: gathers the hands verses as one picture of fear seen in the body

new.text: Fear is aimed at the hands, and the answer is given to the hands
new.beyond_text: sets the frightening of hands beside the strengthening of them

new.text: In Lamentations 4:6 the Hebrew says that hands did not writhe in or on her; the ESV's 'no hands were wrung for her' takes it as grief, and the words also allow that no human hand worked Sodom's fall
new.beyond_text: a translation note: the literal clause beside the rendering, with the two readings the words allow
sources: lexical: H2342A chul, to twist, writhe, from strong_meaning_tree, rendered wrung in this verse

new.text: In 2 Samuel 4:1 the ESV's 'his courage failed' renders 'his hands dropped'
new.beyond_text: a translation note: a body word rendered as an inner word
sources: lexical: H3027I hand (glossed 'courage') with H7503 to slacken

new.text: In the hands verses, what weakens the hands is something heard, and what strengthens them is a word, another person, or God asked to do it
new.beyond_text: reads the cause and the remedy across the verses

new.text: One Hebrew root, chul, is labour pain, trembling, anguish of heart, the dance, the whirling storm and patient waiting
new.beyond_text: sets the uses of one root side by side

new.text: In the siege of Jerusalem a slow death by hunger is called worse than death by the sword
new.beyond_text: joins Lam 4:9 with 4:8 and 4:6 on the lingering

new.text: Under siege the hands of women called compassionate boiled their own children; the verse names when, not why
new.beyond_text: reads the siege as what turned the hands of compassion
